idea: Design a reusable task-expansion skill that, given a tracked task id, produces a 5-section structured overview (what it is / why it matters / upstream-conflict surface / prerequisites / unblocks) consistently across agent sessions. Resolve open design questions: (a) where it lives, (b) invocation surface, (c) prerequisite auto-discovery strategy, (d) output handling / caching, (e) output format.

questionsForSynthesis: Which exact decisions does the expansion improve — task selection, spawn prompt quality, rebase-risk awareness, or operator confidence?
When auto-discovery (git log heuristic) conflicts with operator-curated data.json, which side wins? v1 answer: curated wins; auto-discovery is labeled 'candidates'.
Does the tool enforce schema/evidence, or merely generate best-effort prose? v1 answer: template enforces structure (agent-side); tool only bundles context.
If cached expansions are ever added, what invalidates them and who owns regeneration? v1 answer: no cache.
How does the auto-discovery heuristic decide 'this commit unblocked this task' — task-id match in commit message, same-file touches, or both? v1 answer: both, both labeled as candidates.
